question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A nine days' wonder

options.text: Something that causes only short-lived interest

explanation: A nine days' wonder = चार दिन की चाँदनी। Example: The new gadget was a nine days' wonder and soon forgotten.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A Pyrrhic victory

options.text: A victory in battle by trickery
A victory won at too great a cost
A victory by a narrow margin

explanation: A Pyrrhic victory = हार जैसी महँगी जीत। Example: Winning the case but losing all his savings was a Pyrrhic victory.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A straw in the wind

options.text: A small sign of what may happen

explanation: A straw in the wind = भविष्य का छोटा संकेत। Example: The falling sales were a straw in the wind for the company.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: An ivory tower

options.text: A state of being cut off from practical realities

explanation: An ivory tower = दुनिया की सच्चाइयों से कटी स्थिति। Example: The professor lived in an ivory tower, unaware of ordinary problems.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: At one sitting
explanation: At one sitting = एक ही बैठक में। Example: He finished the whole novel at one sitting.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Be on tenterhooks
explanation: Be on tenterhooks = साँस अटकी रहना। Example: We were on tenterhooks waiting for the result.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Carry coals to Newcastle

options.text: Supply something where it is already plentiful

explanation: Carry coals to Newcastle = उल्टे बाँस बरेली को। Example: Selling tea in Assam is like carrying coals to Newcastle.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Castles in the air
explanation: Castles in the air = हवाई किले बनाना। Example: Stop building castles in the air and start working.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Clip someone's wings
explanation: Clip someone's wings = पर कतरना। Example: Strict rules clipped the young officer's wings.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Cook the books
explanation: Cook the books = हिसाब-किताब में हेराफेरी करना। Example: The manager was caught cooking the books.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: In the doldrums

options.text: In low spirits; inactive or stagnant

explanation: In the doldrums = उदासी या ठहराव में होना। Example: The economy has been in the doldrums for two years.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Keep one's powder dry

options.text: Stay ready but wait for the right moment

explanation: Keep one's powder dry = तैयार रहकर सही समय की प्रतीक्षा करना। Example: Keep your powder dry until the offer is final.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Look a gift horse in the mouth
explanation: Look a gift horse in the mouth = मिले उपहार में कमी निकालना। Example: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth; just say thanks.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Run out of steam
explanation: Run out of steam = जोश ठंडा पड़ जाना। Example: The campaign ran out of steam after a month.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Run the gauntlet

options.text: Face criticism or attack from many people

explanation: Run the gauntlet = चारों ओर से आलोचना झेलना। Example: The minister had to run the gauntlet of angry reporters.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Set one's face against
explanation: Set one's face against = दृढ़ता से विरोध करना। Example: She set her face against the proposal.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: The blind leading the blind
explanation: The blind leading the blind = अंधा अंधे को राह दिखाए। Example: Two beginners teaching each other is the blind leading the blind.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: The jewel in the crown

options.text: The most valuable part of something

explanation: The jewel in the crown = सबसे कीमती हिस्सा। Example: Kashmir is called the jewel in the crown of India.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: The thin end of the wedge

options.text: A small change that leads to bigger harm
The sharp point of a tool

explanation: The thin end of the wedge = बड़े नुकसान की छोटी शुरुआत। Example: Allowing one exception is the thin end of the wedge.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: The tip of the iceberg

options.text: A small visible part of a much bigger problem

explanation: The tip of the iceberg = बड़ी समस्या का छोटा-सा दिखता हिस्सा। Example: The two arrests are only the tip of the iceberg.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Through the roof
explanation: Through the roof = आसमान छूना। Example: Vegetable prices have gone through the roof.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Up in the air
explanation: Up in the air = अधर में लटकना। Example: Our holiday plans are still up in the air.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Within a stone's throw
explanation: Within a stone's throw = दो कदम की दूरी पर। Example: The market is within a stone's throw of my house.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A bad workman always blames his tools

options.text: To blame external factors for poor performance

explanation: A bad workman blames his tools = नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा। Example: He blamed the bat for his duck; a bad workman always blames his tools.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Absence makes the heart grow fonder

options.text: One values someone more when they are away

explanation: Absence makes the heart grow fonder = दूर रहने पर प्रेम और बढ़ता है। Example: After a month abroad, absence made the heart grow fonder.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Bird's eye view

options.text: A wide, general view from above

explanation: Bird's eye view = ऊँचाई से दिखने वाला व्यापक दृश्य। Example: From the hilltop we got a bird's eye view of the city.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Burn bridges

options.text: To destroy chances of returning or going back

explanation: Burn bridges = लौटने के सारे रास्ते नष्ट कर देना। Example: Don't burn bridges with your old employer.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Chew someone out

options.text: To scold or reprimand someone severely

explanation: Chew someone out = कड़ी फटकार लगाना। Example: The coach chewed the players out after the match.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Chew the fat
explanation: Chew the fat = गप्पें लड़ाना। Example: The old friends sat chewing the fat for hours.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Elephantine task
explanation: Elephantine task = बहुत बड़ा और कठिन काम। Example: Preparing the whole syllabus in a month is an elephantine task.
